title: SelectorV1 exploit-SEAL cascade on real KVM: reseed-shifted mid-RNG-exit → NotQuiescent, and retry-forward overshoots staged reseeds
description:
Discovered by task 133 (hm-0paj)'s real-KVM SelectorV1 exploit smoke, AFTER the F3 seal-consistent-env fix cleared the NonAdjacentChain abort. Distinct from F3 (which is the env/cut COORDINATE); this is an entropy × seal-quiescence interaction (task-63/78/132).

MECHANISM (box, seed 7, explore-period 3, deadline-delta 2s):
1. A SelectorV1 EXPLOIT that materializes a FRESH candidate seal (barrier 2) lands the guest mid-RNG-exit at the candidate's V-time: the quiet-reseed (task 78) shifts an RDRAND to coincide with the SDK-event candidate moment, so vmm-core's save_vm_state returns ContractViolation → MachineError::NotQuiescent, and the two-barrier campaign aborts. The SAME V-time (223508107) seals fine in the seed-only explore (step 1) but is non-quiescent in the reseeded exploit (step 2) — proving it is the reseed, not the coordinate.
2. The server contract (vmm-core::control) says the caller should "run a little further and retry" on this (seal_base does exactly that for the base seal), but the two-barrier candidate-seal path (materialize_candidate) does NOT.
3. Adding a naive retry-forward exposes a SECOND blocker: running forward under StopMask::NONE crosses a STAGED reseed Moment (the guest's V-time intercepts are spaced wider than the 1ms retry step, so it overshoots), which the server correctly rejects: "run overshot staged Moment 729310246 (now at V-time 733924708); schedule unsatisfiable".

So the exploit-SEAL path needs a reseed-aware quiescence strategy — e.g. nominate only synchronized/quiescent candidate moments, or a run-forward that stops AT each staged reseed Moment, or seal at the SDK event's synchronized point rather than a raw V-time Deadline. This touches task-63 (seal-rate grid), task-78 (reseed schedule), task-132 (two-barrier). Likely needs a ruling on whether the candidate seal may advance off its nominated Moment.

SCOPE: does NOT block the F3 fix (task 133 deliverable 1/2), which is complete and validated (portable + box: exploit COMPOSES past NonAdjacentChain, campaign completes, bit-identical). Blocks a full SelectorV1 exploit-SEAL box gate (deliverable 3's "seals it"). PureRandom is unaffected (8-branch --repeat 2 passes, hash-neutral).

Priority: P1. Evidence retained in docs/history/IMPLEMENTATION-task133.md + /root/t133-evidence on the box.

comments.author: Paul Hemberger
comments.text: 2026-07-20 window, two more on-silicon substrate findings fixed before first boot (both invisible to the pre-silicon tests): (a) LOADER LAYOUT BUG — a real 6.18 Image carries text_offset 0, so the substrate would have loaded kernel text directly over the reserved params/pvclock low pages, and host clock publications would have overwritten kernel text; every synthetic test image used a nonzero text_offset so the overlap check never fired. Fixed by placing the kernel at a 2MiB-aligned kernel_offset per the arm64 boot protocol (guest patch + 0x40001000 ABI untouched); regression test locks accepted+refused directions. (b) CNTFRQ SEAM UNIMPLEMENTABLE — KVM_GET_ONE_REG(3,3,14,0,0) is ENOENT on real KVM (6.8 live; absent from pinned 6.18.35 sysreg table): guest CNTFRQ is now read as the host's own EL0 CNTFRQ_EL0. BONUS negative control retained: linux-boot on the stock host now fails exactly at mechanism attestation ('refusing to fall back to the stock signal kick'), proving the gate cannot green without the patched kernel. -aa3preempt kernel deb BUILT+INSTALLED, GRUB default pinned to stock 6.8 (saved_entry), one-shot grub-reboot planned; -aa4guard building.

comments.author: Paul Hemberger
comments.text:
2026-07-20 LIVE GATE RESULTS on 6.18.35-aa3preempt (patched host, build-id verified, KVM_EXIT_PREEMPT mechanism attested — stock-host negative control fails closed at mechanism attestation, proving no silent fallback):

AA-5(c) BOOT: PASS. Guest boots to userspace, HARMONY_AA5_CLOCKSOURCE_OK + HARMONY_AA5_READY, no RCU stalls, 21k exits, ~1s. Pinned pvclock GPA 0x40001000, 3 publications, clockevent asserted+ACKed. NOTE: skid_margin=53 (the AA-1 constant) OVERSHOOTS on the Linux guest — arm-early Preempt lands ~56 events past target; needs headroom. Boot succeeds at --skid-margin 1024. This is a Linux-guest landing-headroom finding, NOT an AA-1 skid error (bare payloads land within 53).

AA-5(c) SAME-SEED x2 STATE IDENTITY: DIVERGENCE FOUND (state_digest differs). Localized: console bit-identical, registers bit-identical (regs_only digest matches across runs), ONLY guest RAM diverges — 485 bytes / 256MB, clustered in kernel CRNG state (base_crng, input_pool) + some .data. Negative control (differing --refresh-delta) correctly flagged as mismatch by the identity checker.

AA-5(b) EL0 CNTVCT CLOSURE: HOLE FOUND (el0probe boot emits HARMONY_AA5_EL0_LIVE_COUNTER_HOLE — userspace EL0 CNTVCT read observes a moving counter). ROOT CAUSE (proven): the pvclock patch closes EL0 counter access only in the driver's arch_counter_set_user_access() (boot CPU setup), but arch/arm64/kernel/process.c update_cntkctl_el1() reasserts ARCH_TIMER_USR_VCT_ACCESS_EN (bit1) on every thread switch unless an erratum/TSC_SIGSEGV workaround applies — none do on N1. Landed guest CNTKCTL_EL1=0x2 confirms EL0VCTEN set. This same live EL0/adjacent counter access is the likely source of the CRNG entropy divergence above. Fix in progress: patch update_cntkctl_el1 to force EL0 counter denial under CONFIG_HARMONY_ARM_PVCLOCK, rebuild guest kernel, re-run both gates. Raw evidence in results/aa-5/live-20260720/.

comments.author: Paul Hemberger
comments.text:
2026-07-20 AA-5(c) LIVE VERDICT (evidence committed: spikes/arm-altra/results/aa-5/live-20260720/, README.md has the full table + root-cause chain):

PARAVIRT-CLOCK MECHANISM = PROVEN on N1:
- Boot to userspace + steady state PASS (CLOCKSOURCE_OK, READY, no RCU stall).
- Same-seed CONSOLE bit-identical PASS. Same-seed REGISTER digest bit-identical PASS (regs_only matches; only RAM differs).
- Counter closure PASS: vmlinux has 0 raw cntvct reads; all counter access page-routed.
- AA-5(b) EL0 CNTVCT closure PASS after fix: trapped EL0 read emulated through the page (EL0_CNTVCT_PAGE_OK).
- Mechanism attestation: stock-host control fails closed at 'refusing to fall back to signal kick' — no silent fallback.

FULL-STATE (RAM) IDENTITY = CHARACTERIZED RESIDUAL, not closed. Same-seed runs diverge ONLY in kernel CRNG (base_crng/input_pool/ptr_key), 400-700 bytes/256MB, non-reproducible => live entropy. Root cause chained on-box: base_crng reseeds a deterministic NUMBER of times (same generation) but with nondeterministic INPUT (different key). Closed 2 channels: (1) jitter harvester try_to_generate_entropy (wall-clock hrtimer) via credited /chosen/rng-seed + a harmony_pvclock_ready guard so the early seed-credit path doesn't fault on the not-yet-mapped page; (2) add_interrupt_randomness interrupt-PC jitter skipped under CONFIG_HARMONY_ARM_PVCLOCK. Residual remains (reseed/workqueue timing jitter vs the exact-landing digest Moment). This is the 'bursty entropy' hard problem, orthogonal to the clock: the work clock makes retired-branch execution deterministic but the CRNG deliberately harvests microarch jitter the work clock doesn't model. => needs an explicit entropy-closure contract row for the deterministic guest (analogous to counter closure), recorded as remaining build.

6 findings fixed+committed this session (see also earlier comment): scanner binutils-2.42 self-check; overlapping-patch pristine re-extract; loader 2MiB kernel offset (real Image text_offset=0 would overlap pvclock page); CNTFRQ read via host EL0 (no KVM one-reg); EL0 thread-switch closure (update_cntkctl_el1); + the 3 entropy-closure patches. Skid note: AA-1 skid_margin=53 overshoots on the Linux guest (~56 past target); boots at --skid-margin 1024 (landing-headroom item, not an AA-1 error).

title: Make Nimbus TTL admission cost-driven instead of preset-driven
description: TTL is caller intent, not an enforced owner restriction. Humans and agents choose --ttl (and extension duration) based on how long they expect to need a machine; Nimbus records the resulting expiry so nimbusd can sweep it. Admission enforcement must be exclusively cost-based: pessimistic authorized lease cost, per-lease cost ceiling, outstanding exposure, hourly burn, and daily/monthly authorization budgets. Presets describe reviewed hardware, provider, region, image, modes, and frozen pricing, with no machine-specific max_ttl. Remove global/preset TTL rejection from create and extend paths, schemas, pricing snapshots, output, docs, and compatibility handling while retaining bounded duration parsing/arithmetic and rejecting values whose computed quote overflows or exceeds cost policy. Test ad-hoc TTLs, extensions, hourly increments, minimum charges, zero/invalid live-provider rates, overflow, cost rejection, expiry persistence, and sweeper cleanup.
close_reason: Implemented cost-only TTL admission: removed TTL ceilings from policy/presets/snapshots/output, preserved legacy input compatibility, added positive duration pricing for enabled live presets, and atomically enforced cumulative per-lease extension cost. Nimbus full gate: 189 passed, 85.14% coverage, build passed; live nimbusd verification passed.

title: Integrate Harmony with Cumulo-managed nimbusd
description: Build a daemon-backed Nimbus thin client for Harmony, deploy a self-sweeping nimbusd from private Cumulo, and expose only the Nimbus skill/client capability in Harmony. Provider credentials, configuration, metadata, and admin authority must never enter Harmony or GitHub.
design: Cumulo runs one self-sweeping nimbusd. Same-host Harmony clients use an owner-private Unix-domain socket with operator-only authority and no client credential; admin is unavailable on that transport. Authenticated HTTP remains optional for remote deployments. Provider credentials remain exclusively in Cumulo and are resolved only inside nimbusd. nimbusd performs a blocking startup sweep and supervised periodic sweeps.
acceptance_criteria: Nimbus CLI fails closed into either private local-socket mode or authenticated remote mode; local socket sends no bearer credential and cannot call admin; nimbusd owns startup and periodic sweeps; Cumulo runs one daemon service and Harmony receives only the socket launcher; read-only presets, doctor, and budget work from the Harmony repository; no provider mutation or ARM lease occurs before explicit green light; no credential values are read, printed, staged, or committed.
notes: Final credential containment: Cumulo defaults to Keychain service op-service-account-harmony, op confirms SERVICE_ACCOUNT identity, and scripts/exec-without-op-token removes OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN before nimbusd starts. launchd service is running with one op parent and one nimbusd child; final startup sweep completed at 2026-07-17T13:29:57Z. Harmony read-only doctor is 5/5 green, budget shows admission disabled and zero spend, and inventory is empty. Final Cumulo gitleaks directory scan reports no leaks.

title: Paravirt work-derived clock: design spec (ARM correctness + x86 perf)
description: Design doc for routing guest time reads through a work-derived paravirtual clock page (kvmclock-shaped, V-time/work as the source) instead of trapping counter reads. Dual justification: (a) MANDATORY for the ARM vendor port — no reachable ARM server chip has FEAT_ECV (Altra/N1 is v8.2; Graviton 3=V1, Graviton 4/Grace=V2 all lack it; it only arrives with AmpereOne and the V3/N3 wave), so guest CNTVCT trapping is unavailable and we must prevent the guest from executing raw counter reads at all — we own the guest kernel; (b) x86 performance — removes RDTSC exits from the hot path (the nested-x86 N-4 memo's sizing recommendation). One design serving both axes. Spec only: page layout, update discipline (when does the vmm refresh it), determinism argument (values derived from work, never wall time), the raw-instruction closure story per arch (x86: keep RDTSC trap as backstop; ARM: contract-level denial/undef of raw counter access), and the migration path for the existing x86 VClock. Implementation is a separate bead after ratification.

title: Differential observation/materialization migration (coordinator epic)
description: Coordinator-only epic for the Differential observation/materialization migration ruled by docs/DISSONANCE-STRATEGY.md; never implement as one patch. Children own SDK normalization, lineage/evidence-cut/retention economics spike, explicit GO ratification, deterministic Revision coordination, atomic seal-cut capture across the VM control seam, generic Explorer/evidence-ledger/two-pass archive integration, and production retention/completeness policy. The epic closes only after every child and each child-owned migration gate closes; the later cooperative maze gate hm-cs5 deliberately begins after the epic and is not an epic-close prerequisite. A spike NO-GO blocks or supersedes DD-specific production children and retargets backend-independent seal-cut capture under the selected alternative unless actual-seal admission is explicitly abandoned.
design: Use production differential-dataflow initially with one Timely worker. Revision numbers committed input updates; proposal mappings persist before dispatch, issue order is seeded, cohorts freeze their input, and failure cannot create frontier holes. Evidence identity includes campaign/config, rollout, source, site/property where applicable, Moment, and explicit source ordinal. The initial cut-addressable stream is the ordered SDK vector; its seal carries (Moment, included SDK-event count) atomically in the snapshot response, and vector positions below count are included. Current serial scrape is source-local/stop-granular and cannot drive seal-relative cells or cross-source sequence. sdk-events normalizes ordinary assertions, exact extremal guidance, and internal binary declarations without guessing unresolved v1 state. No host floating point is state-affecting. Split immutable evidence, bounded working membership, provisional unsealed transitions, committed Entry cells, archive retention, and finalized facts. Generic Explorer durably appends completed evidence, consumes provisional transitions, schedules budgeted replay, holds a temporary seal, submits the later seal revision, then keeps/drops after the second barrier. TraceStore is referenced payload backing, not ledger authority. Direct recomputation is an oracle, not a second backend.
acceptance_criteria: Both SDK ingress fixtures persist declarations, site/property identity, normalized events, raw unknown/number tokens, ordering scope, revision mapping, lineage, and evidence cuts. Snapshot/control goldens bind each successful seal to its synchronized Moment and SDK prefix count; failed seals yield no cut. V1 never-fired state remains non-reducible; wire v2 or explicit instrumentation covers production state; set/max/min/accumulate and configured history use exact deterministic values; mixed operations/shapes and malformed input fail totally. Serial scrape remains full-run evidence until capture-time stamping exists and is rejected from seal-relative cell and cross-source sequence queries. The first pass emits non-authoritative transitions only; sibling keys, half-open same-Moment cuts, canonical order, actual-seal cells, two-revision materialization, temporary-seal lifetime, and quality domination are tested. Genesis replay equals cached lineage plus suffix. Restart rebuilds from the durable ledger and referenced payloads; working membership cannot change committed Entry cells/finalized facts; Entry eviction is separate; GC checkpoints state supported queries. Input/worker permutation, crash recovery, and cohorts produce identical artifacts with no frontier skip. Occurrence counterexamples aggregate by property over one immutable completed-run evidence view while site coverage stays separate; absence expectations use finalized property counts. Legacy LinkSensor/channel packing and mutable Archive::admit are absent. Standard gates pass on macOS/Linux.
notes: 2026-07-12 review rulings: normalize both LAYERS ingress formats into persisted evidence. Ordinary Antithesis assertions are non-fail-stop property events; numeric guidance declares SDK-filtered extrema, never arbitrary current set. Preserve raw number tokens and require bounded exact non-floating ordering before state use. Binary v1 never-fired state is reportable but non-reducible; wire v2 declares production state. Evidence identity separates rollout/source/site/property/Moment/ordinal. SDK seals use a server-stamped (Moment, full SDK-prefix count) cut and lineage composition; other sources need their own cursor, and current console scrape is terminal-only evidence. Immutable evidence, bounded working membership, provisional unsealed transitions, committed Entry cells, archive retention, and finalized facts are separate. Revisions use persisted seeded issue order with deterministic crash/failure/cohort rules. Generic Explorer owns durable evidence append, the two-barrier replay, and temporary-seal lifecycle; hm-bbx.6 owns physical cut capture. Oracle remains pure completed-run judgment over an immutable ledger-backed view. Occurrence counterexamples and finalized must-hit absence expectations are separate property-level views. Sensor/Feature/Channel, LinkSensor, CellFnV1 behavior, and mutable Archive::admit are compatibility paths, not production interfaces.

title: PAUL: ratify a CellFn from REKEY-REPORT.md's ranked menu (or decline)
description:
tasks/97 (bead hm-b3h) delivered dissonance/benchmark/REKEY-REPORT.md: the E-fails playbook's steps 2-4, run over the frozen GO/NO-GO #2 trace corpus. Playbook step 4 is 'a human picks from the ranked candidates' — docs/SCORING.md R2 is explicit that auto-tuning only ever proposes. The harness deliberately promotes nothing.

The menu (top three distinct proposals, primary slice bug3-campaign):
  1. draw-top-64      — v1 + a chosen sparse state channel on the entropy draw's top byte, folded mod 64. Ranks first because 65.7 cells/campaign sits on the stated target T=64.
  2. v1-shipped       — keep the status quo. Indistinguishable from the ENTIRE fold_k/Quant/lastnew knob space on this corpus.
  9. draw-top-256     — the same channel, unfolded (259 cells pooled).

What Paul needs to weigh, and what the report will not decide for him:
- The harness's one bug-based axis (chain preservation, law 6) is VACUOUS on this corpus: every finding chain's proper ancestors are branch 0, so even the one-cell 'no-channels' floor passes it. The ranking therefore rests entirely on the two discovery-curve axes that law 6 disqualifies as sole evidence.
- The trigger-blind twin control (draw-low-256) matches draw-top-256 on every quantity a search could use, on the unsteered ablation slice. Where they differ, the BLIND one looks broader. No offline axis separates a bug-aligned descriptor from a bug-blind one.
- The ranking is a function of the STATED target T. At T=64 the order is draw-top-64 -> v1-shipped -> foldk-16; at T=256 it becomes draw-top-256 -> draw-top-only-256 -> draw-low-256. Choosing T is a human judgment about how much search energy a cell should get.
- Ratifying a draw-* candidate is a bet on IJON's thesis (some projection of a guest's chosen state correlates with some class of trigger), not evidence that this projection does.
acceptance_criteria: Paul records a ruling: which candidate (if any) is ratified, and the stated target T. A decline is a valid outcome — the report's own recommendation is a SEQUENCING, not a candidate. The ruling unblocks the bounded box confirmation.

title: W3 — committed evidence must recompute its verdict
description:
WORK ORDER W3 — committed evidence must recompute its verdict.

Live verdicts across aa-2/aa-4/aa-5/aa-6 are content-addressed ON THE BOX; the repo carries
only hashes and conclusions. A checkout cannot independently recompute what the gate decided.
Adjacent instances: a checker whose inputs were never committed (hm-of6t F12 commits 0
console.bin), a shard script depending on an uncommitted environment.json (hm-q1z), an
overflow check that cannot be regenerated for the run it graded (hm-5a6 forward half, owned
by W1).

Same root cause as the AA-3 pin-fragility saga: verified results whose proof lives on machines
that no longer exist. hm-gfr1 (reproducible box + toolchain definition) and hm-nji6
(reproducible payload builds + archived certified binaries) are the infrastructure half of
this contract, not separate projects — they are what makes the ARM and AMD parking lots
re-runnable at all after a wipe or a machine swap.

Consolidated 2026-07-24. Deliverable: one evidence-retention contract (what must be committed
for a verdict to be independently recomputable), one retention policy applied across the
results trees, one checker that enforces it.

title: W2 — one definition of executable code (static scan vs runtime guard)
description:
WORK ORDER W2 — one definition of executable code.

The static ELF scanner and the page-granular runtime execute-guard disagree about what
counts as code. Every child is a symptom of that single disagreement, not an independent
defect.

The consequence is not cosmetic: the full AA-5(c) Linux guest CANNOT currently boot under
the AA-4 execute-guard (hm-fcod) because the guard flags kernel alternative-patching DATA
that shares an executable .init page during early boot — the runtime analog of the static
.rodata false positive the section-aware scanner already excludes. Two features that each
pass their own gate do not compose.

Consolidated 2026-07-24. Solve the seam once — a shared decoder/definition consulted by
both the static scan and the runtime guard, or a guest layout where no data-bearing page
is executable — and the hardening items below stop being a list.

NOTE: hm-7o68 and hm-7np are multi-finding beads; their input-bounds sub-items (hm-7np
scan-bound) overlap W4 and travel with whichever lands first.

title: exact-arrival arm misses staged Moments on pvclock guests when the rollout leg spans a clock-refresh boundary (maze @3e7 repro)
description:
Found by task 134 M2 (hm-qcpp) box validation on hetzner (2026-07-22), surfaced
once the per-branch rolling deadline gave maze SelectorV1 exploits their full
span. Does NOT block M2 (Paul ruled Option (a): accept @1e7; this is its own
bug, NOT a silent fold into hm-x1ss).

## Symptom

A maze SelectorV1 exploit rollout run (StopMask::NONE, single deadline
origin+delta) with delta = 3e7 (multi-quantum) fails: the server refuses with
`control error: run overshot staged Moment <M> (now at V-time <M'>);
schedule unsatisfiable`. The exact-arrival machinery expected the run to STOP
exactly at the staged reseed Moment M (drain it), but the run sailed past to the
next intercept-grid boundary M' — overshooting by < 1 quantum.

## Box data points (both EXIT 1; lease maze-qcpp-3e7, reverted to stock)

- @3e7 as-configured (marker window == deadline_delta): overshot staged Moment
  237012404, stopped at 244341956 (overshoot +7,329,552 ns ≈ 0.7 quantum).
- @3e7 option-(b) (marker window bounded to one intercept quantum 10_416_667,
  decoupled from deadline_delta): STILL overshoots, at an earlier marker
  191224419 → 192258621 (+1,034,202 ns). **Option-(b) does NOT fix it** — the
  overshoot is not a marker-PLACEMENT problem; a multi-quantum leg crosses ANY
  staged reseed without an exact-arrival stop.
- Counter (@1e7, one-quantum): green, 11/11 exploits drained an in-window reseed
  at exact Moments, bit-identical — because the single deadline stop lands within
  one grid step and drains the marker there.

## Why "multi-quantum ⇒ overshoot" is FALSE in general (the key discriminator)

#138 (hm-esfd) re-materialized MULTI-QUANTUM candidate-seal legs with mid-leg
reseed markers drained BIT-IDENTICALLY on the 2s game path (deadline-delta 2e9,
~192 quanta). So multi-quantum legs are NOT inherently broken. The failing
ingredient is specific to the maze being a **pvclock guest** (task-110 paravirt
clock; the ~10,416,667 ns quantum IS the guest's pvclock refresh grid). The game
path's intercept grid is not pvclock-refresh-anchored the same way, so its
exact-arrival arm hits the staged Moments; the maze's does not when the leg
crosses a pvclock clock-refresh boundary.

## Concrete suspect (leading hypothesis, NOT a conclusion)

The control.rs run-loop arms `vmm.arm_arrival(m)` for each staged Moment and
**drops the bool return**. `arm_arrival` silently DECLINES (returns false, no-op)
when `work_for_vns(m) < last_intercept_work`. Hypothesis: after a pvclock
re-anchor (skid correction) the vns<->work conversion disagrees with the
published `effective_vns`; a future staged Moment maps to a work value below the
current anchor, so the arm silently no-ops; the guest then free-runs to the next
natural boundary and overshoots by < 1 quantum (the observed +7.3e6 ns).
Verify by logging the arm_arrival bool + the (vns, work, effective_vns) triple
at each staged-Moment arm on the failing @3e7 leg.

## Fix direction (determinism-core — NOT the hm-qcpp maze-vertical mandate)

The rollout run must marker-clamp staged reseeds like materialize_candidate
already does for the seal (stop AT each staged Moment, drain, continue), and/or
arm_arrival's decline path must not be silently dropped on a pvclock guest.
Design home is hm-x1ss (schedule-closure). hm-sp8v (the ARM conducted
async-event delivery / arm_arrival port) should INHERIT this finding — the same
exact-arrival arm is being ported to ARM.

## Edges

- discovered-from / provenance: hm-qcpp (maze M2).
- design home: hm-x1ss (schedule-closure root cause).
- must inherit: hm-sp8v (ARM arm_arrival port).

## Follow-up (note, don't build here)

A loud maze-driver rejection of deadline_delta > ~one pvclock quantum is a
sensible guard (the accepted regime under Paul's Option (a); see the M2 doctrine
note in docs/history/IMPLEMENTATION-task134.md).

THE BUG STAYS OPEN: the @3e7 overshoot is an unexplained contract violation (limitation-vs-clobber-vs-never-armed undischarged — see hm-x1ss note); the CURE is the hm-x1ss schedule-closure decision; portable red needs hm-40na. Next concrete step: run the discrimination runbook on the x86 box when reachable.

title: Statically/reproducibly define box hardware + toolchain (NixOS or similar) so spikes survive box wipes + machine swaps
description:
Paul directive 2026-07-22. The AA-3 pin-fragility saga (voided cert -> the whole regenerated-pin-basis question) traces to a root gap: we have no static, reproducible, code-defined description of the hardware + toolchain environment we certify on. When the box is wiped or swapped to a different physical machine, the toolchain reinstalls at a different version and the build environment shifts, so certified artifact BYTES become non-reproducible -> every wipe forces a fresh integrity-basis decision instead of just reconstructing the certified environment.

Investigate a declarative, static hardware/environment definition -- NixOS or equivalent (declarative OS config + pinned toolchain + reproducible/hermetic builds + pinned kernel/module set) -- so a spike's environment is captured AS CODE and reconstructable bit-identically on any machine.

Complements hm-nji6 (reproducible payload pins): hm-nji6 makes the payload BUILD reproducible; this makes the whole BOX ENVIRONMENT reproducible. Together they'd let a re-cert reconstruct the exact certified environment (host kernel build-id, rustc version, build paths, module set) rather than re-litigate an integrity basis every wipe. Deliverable: a spike/proposal evaluating NixOS (or Guix / a pinned-container + IaC alternative) for the harmony box fleet, with the reproducibility guarantees named.

title: AA-3 payload-pin fragility: make payload builds reproducible + archive the certified binaries (survive box wipe / machine swap)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (task 137, ARM AA-3 re-cert, 2026-07-22): the cert byte-pins the payload BUILD OUTPUT (--payload-pins = sha256 of each compiled binary), which is fragile to toolchain+environment. After the 2026-07-20 box wipe (rustc reinstalled to 1.97.1) + a DIFFERENT physical Altra, rebuilding the IDENTICAL git-verified source yields DIFFERENT bytes (compiler codegen differs by rustc version; the build path is baked into debug-info/panic strings). So the committed byte-pins can't be matched by any rebuild, and arm-spike REQUIRES pins to run -> the re-cert is blocked on an integrity-basis decision (the same class the GO was VOIDED over). Payloads are BEHAVIORALLY identical (count-exactness / work==target is byte-pin-independent; the smoke proved the mechanism).

FIX (recommended = 1+2 together): (1) REPRODUCIBLE/HERMETIC payload builds — pin the exact toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml), --remap-path-prefix to normalize the build path, strip/normalize debug-info; then identical source -> identical bytes on ANY machine and the byte-pin becomes source-derived + wipe-proof while still catching a silent payload swap. (2) ARCHIVE the certified BINARIES (LFS / artifact store), not just their hashes, so a re-cert can re-run the EXACT cert bytes without rebuilding. Optional: (3) containerize the cert build env (pinned Docker toolchain) so it survives a box wipe; (4) pin the SEMANTIC contract (instruction-count/oracle) rather than raw bytes. Prevents the NEXT re-cert from being blocked by a wipe/machine-change. Does NOT change the current parked AA-3 basis decision (Paul's ruling) — this is the durable prevention. Related: hm-idb, tasks/137.

title: Can the 'unsafe snapshot moment' CLASS be eliminated at the root (schedule-closure) — or is hm-esfd's run-forward permanent?
description:
FOLLOW-UP to the hm-esfd ruling (Paul-adopted 2026-07-21: Option C, 'a candidate seal may advance off its nominated Moment to the first fully-drained quiescent boundary' — the run-forward / 'wait a beat then snap' workaround). That fix unblocks both frontier verticals (SelectorV1 exploit-seal, maze M2) and is the shipped fix. This bead tracks Paul's standing concern: is the EXISTENCE of unsafe moments fundamentally unavoidable, or designable-away — i.e. is run-forward a PERMANENT design element or a BRIDGE?

THE FRAMING (via the entropy-closure ruling's INPUT-closure vs SCHEDULE-closure split): an unsafe moment is a SCHEDULE-closure residual — at the snapshot's target V-time Moment the guest is mid-way through a host round-trip (a CRNG reseed / RDRAND / hypercall-doorbell OUT), so it can't be cleanly frozen. INPUT-closure (seed-pure deterministic CRNG, hm-kz9v) closes the entropy VALUES but NOT the delivery schedule. hm-sp8v (ARM conducted async-event delivery / arm_arrival port — the async-delivery-at-a-deterministic-Moment machinery proven on the x86 host-plane in task 59) is scoped to close the CRNG *schedule* residual for ALL kernel state.

THE QUESTION TO EVALUATE (deliverable = a written design verdict):
1. Does conducted/schedule-closed delivery (hm-sp8v-style) ELIMINATE the unsafe-moment class, or merely make it DETERMINISTIC/PREDICTABLE? If the latter, that is itself powerful: predictable unsafe moments make 'nominate only synchronized Moments' (the option-B Fable rejected as unpredictable) VIABLE, and make run-forward trivially deterministic. So schedule-closure may retire run-forward OR make option B work — decide which.
2. Is the in-flight-window class CRNG-only, or structural to ANY host round-trip (device I/O, other doorbell OUTs, interrupts)? If structural, run-forward (or a quiescent-by-construction delivery model) is needed regardless of entropy determinism.
3. Cost/benefit: run-forward is cheap (~one client fn) but leaves the re-materialization determinism surface (hm-esfd's blocking sub-gate); schedule-closure is a deeper guest/host-delivery change but yields snapshots quiescent-by-construction. Which does the frontier ultimately want?
4. Recommend: keep run-forward permanently, retire it after schedule-closure lands (hm-sp8v), or a hybrid.

NOT blocking — hm-esfd run-forward is the shipped fix. This is a design-direction evaluation, conceptually downstream of the ARM control-plane / delivery-plane work (hm-sp8v depends on ARM control-plane bring-up).
notes: PR #145 CONFIRMED input (judge-verified by mutation, 2026-07-23): the genuine late-landing shape is refused POST-STEP by the drain's crossed-marker clause (ScheduleUnsatisfiable) — the PR #143 arm-site ScheduleMomentUnreachable guard is INERT on this shape (arm-time predicate, exact clock keeps arrival_vns()==m; it covers only the clock-coarseness class). The schedule-closure design therefore owns BOTH: (a) whether a bounded-late drain can make multi-quantum pvclock legs safe, and (b) whether arm-site coverage of the physically-late class needs a production seam change. Portable red now exists (PR #145 tests + the documented drain-clause mutation).

title: AA-5 guest × AA-4 execute-guard: runtime guard flags .init alternative-data on execute
description: Discovered 2026-07-21 booting the full AA-5(c) Linux guest under the AA-4 stage-2 execute-guard (linux-boot --stage2-exec-guard, an untested combination beyond the 2026-07-20 scope). The guard rejected page 0x4041d000 (gen 56) with 7 exclusives at a regular 0x54-byte stride = the kernel .altinstr_replacement/.altinstructions alternative-fallback DATA that shares the executable .init PT_LOAD and is mapped executable during early boot. This is the runtime analog of the static .rodata false-positive the section-aware scanner now excludes (hm-jth/hm-7o68-F3): the static scan correctly treats it as non-code, but the raw page-granular runtime guard (by design does not trust section metadata) flags it. So AA-5 guest cannot currently boot UNDER the AA-4 guard. AA-4 (bare planted proofs) and AA-5(c) (Linux guest) were always separate gates; this is a new combination. Fix options: teach the runtime guard the same .init-data section-awareness, OR lay out the guest so no data-bearing page is executable (page-separate .init.text from .altinstructions like the payload rodata fix). Evidence: spikes/arm-altra/results/aa-4/live-20260721/finding-guest-under-guard.out + README. NOT an AA-4 mechanism gate failure (6 mechanism gates all PASS). Parent: hm-rfz.

title: wire-v2 MustHit satisfactions never clear the absence view (satisfies_must_hit keys on the v1 verb)
description: Found by task 134 (hm-cs5), the first wire-v2 cooperative vertical. explorer::occurrence::satisfies_must_hit accepts a satisfaction only when the event's assert_type is Some(Sometimes)/Some(Reachable) — the wire-v1 VERB, populated only by v1 catalog parsing. A wire-v2 catalog deliberately carries no verb (only an Expectation), so decode_assert yields Payload::Assertion{assert_type: None, condition: Some(true)} for a MustHit HIT, satisfies_must_hit returns false, and AbsenceLedger keeps the property listed as a never-satisfied absence forever. Every v2-declared MustHit point (the maze goal marker; any future v2 workload) misreports as a held absence even after it fires. The maze driver works around it by folding goal hits host-side from the same committed evidence (MazeCampaignOutcome::goal_hits is the authoritative witness) and documents the divergence on MazeCampaignOutcome::open_expectations. Likely fix shape (needs a ruling on which side owns it): satisfies_must_hit should also accept (declared expectation == MustHit && condition == Some(true)) via the schema entry, mirroring what decode_assert already enforces for disposition consistency; or sdk-events could surface the expectation on the event. Repro: campaign-runner tests maze_campaign::two_barrier_evidence_path_end_to_end with a goal-reaching seed — camp.absences().satisfied(goal) stays 0 while goal events with condition=Some(true) sit in the committed evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A v2-declared MustHit point whose HIT evaluation is committed clears its absence (satisfied count > 0); the maze driver's open_expectations doc-workaround note is removed; existing v1 behavior unchanged (verb check still authoritative for v1); regression test covering the v2 shape in explorer::occurrence.

title: Seed-pure deterministic CRNG for the ARM guest (HARMONY_DETERMINISTIC_CRNG) — entropy INPUT-closure build
description: RULED 2026-07-20 (Paul adopted Fable 5 xhigh consultation; entropy-closure decision). The authorized entropy INPUT-closure build — the entropy analogue of the counter-closure row. Mechanism: a HARMONY_DETERMINISTIC_CRNG guest-kernel config making the CRNG a PURE FUNCTION of the credited seed — (1) base_crng key KDF'd from /chosen/rng-seed; (2) reseed-from-input_pool disabled outright (NOT a deterministic ratchet — which consumer sees key_n vs key_{n+1} is still schedule-dependent); (3) add_interrupt_randomness + jitter mixing compiled out entirely (a live-but-unread pool still dirties the full-RAM digest). KASLR: derive /chosen/kaslr-seed from the campaign seed (substitution, NOT nokaslr-ban — layout becomes an explored input dimension the Reproducer pins). PROOF/acceptance = an entropy-reachability gate: 0 reachable entropy-mix sites in vmlinux under the config (the analogue of '0 raw CNTVCT'), plus a NEW full-RAM-digest-identity sub-gate for AA-5(c). Contract consequence: randomness is deterministic-per-Reproducer + unpredictable to workload adversaries; secrecy-from-harness is out of contract (Reproducers are secret-bearing; test workloads only). Sharpens the CRNG canary rather than silencing it — post-patch, any residual full-RAM divergence is a genuine schedule leak, not amplifier noise. Sibling: the SCHEDULE residual is NOT this bead (see the delivery-lane bead).

comments.author: Paul Hemberger
comments.text: FABLE 5 xhigh CONSULTATION (2026-07-20, input for Paul's ruling — NOT itself the ruling). Headline: the CRNG residual is NOT an entropy problem — it is the async-delivery SCHEDULE gap wearing an entropy costume; split it. Decompose 'entropy' into (1) harvest INPUTS (jitter loop, interrupt-PC, cycle reads) = counter-shaped, closable by the substitution template = ALREADY DONE on-box; (2) harvest SCHEDULE (how many interrupts mixed before the reseed workqueue runs) = different in kind, = the arm_arrival/deliver-at-a-Moment machinery harmony already owns from the x86 host-plane work. The CRNG is a deliberate hash-accumulator that AMPLIFIES a one-interrupt schedule difference into full-key divergence + never forgets => it is the most sensitive schedule-nondeterminism CANARY; option B (build conducted-delivery for the CRNG's sake) is backwards. RECOMMENDATION: (A) scoped as 'seed-pure CRNG' under (C)'s contract framing, AA-5(c) scoped per (D). Mechanism: HARMONY_DETERMINISTIC_CRNG config — base_crng key KDF'd from /chosen/rng-seed; reseed-from-input_pool disabled (NOT a deterministic ratchet — which-consumer-sees-which-key is still schedule-dependent); add_interrupt_randomness/jitter mixing compiled out (a live-but-unread pool still dirties the digest). PROOF = entropy-reachability gate: 0 reachable entropy-mix sites in vmlinux (the analogue of '0 raw CNTVCT'). Sharpens the canary, doesn't silence it. KASLR: deterministic /chosen/kaslr-seed derived from campaign seed, NOT nokaslr-ban ('substitution not amputation'; layout becomes an explored input dimension; nokaslr = degenerate today-simplification, wrong as contract term). REAL WORKLOADS: no contradiction — unpredictability is adversary-relative; seed-derived ChaCha20 satisfies TLS (net adversary lacks the seed); a Reproducer records full RAM so it already holds the key => secrecy-from-harness is out of contract, Reproducers are secret-bearing (test workloads only). This is the settled DST position (FDB/Antithesis run TLS deterministically). AA-5(c) CLAIMS NOW: clock mechanism deterministic on N1 (console+regs bit-identical under pinned layout) + counter-closure holds + entropy INPUT-closure demonstrated + residual characterized as SCHEDULE-borne not clock-borne; does NOT claim full-RAM identity. AUTHORIZES: (1) HARMONY_DETERMINISTIC_CRNG patch + entropy-reachability gate + kaslr-seed plumbing + full-RAM-digest-identity sub-gate as acceptance; (2) schedule-closure stays in the DELIVERY lane (ARM control-plane port), NOT re-filed as entropy work. Full text: session scratchpad fable-entropy-ruling.md.

title: Negative-control planted-failure fixtures mandatory for every spike/campaign evidence gate (CI must go red)
description:
WORK ORDER W1 — every grader must be able to fail.

Umbrella for the grader-integrity family. Ten independently-confirmed findings across
the ARM (PR #132/#135) and AMD (PR #128) reviews are the same defect species in six
files: a check that returns green without having actually checked anything. None
falsified a shipped result — each was re-verified by hand against retained evidence —
but collectively the gates are weaker than their names promise.

Consolidated 2026-07-24 because every child independently asks for the SAME deliverable
(a planted-failure fixture that makes CI go red), and the fixture harness is written
once rather than ten times.

DISCIPLINE: a grader without a negative-control fixture proving it can go red is not a
gate. Each child ships its fix plus the fixture that would have caught it.

Files in scope: host/aa1c-determinism-check.py, host/aa3-determinism-compare.py,
schemas/floor-check/src/check.rs, spikes/amd-epyc/host/check-floors.py,
spikes/amd-epyc/harness/ae0-probe.c, spikes/amd-epyc/harness/singlestep-driver.c.
notes: Future work (Paul greenlit 2026-07-18). Every spike/campaign evidence gate ships with planted-failure fixtures in CI: mutate one retained-transcript byte / drop one sample point / corrupt one digest → the gate MUST go red. Rationale: a gate never seen to fail is unproven — harmony's own core doctrine (campaigns prove themselves by finding planted bugs) applied to the evidence pipeline itself. Motivated by TWO green-on-fail escapes in one week: PR #132 (headline AA-3 co-tenant MATCH shipped on a determinism comparator that was NEVER invoked; see hm-gzp) and nested-x86 PR #98. A negative control catches both. Scope: floor-check / campaign success-marker gates across all spikes (ARM AA-*, AMD tasks/123, nested-x86 re-cert, differential). Companion ideas from the same Fable review (NOT filed — Paul greenlit only planted-failures; recorded for reference): (a) PASS markers only written by checkers, exit-0 is never evidence; (b) comparators assert coverage (full join, print join cardinality); (c) path-based contract-change tripwire lint; (d) grep audit of every campaign for the marker-on-exit-0 + intersection-join idiom.

title: Have nimbusd maintain SSH aliases for active leases

title: W^X + rescan-on-exec: vmm-side executable-page tracking for the counter-opcode reachability gate
description: The third rung of the PARAVIRT-CLOCK.md §3.3 enforcement ladder (kernel-config guarantee → static opcode scan → W^X + rescan-on-exec), accepted as specced-and-stubbed at the task-110 review (foreman ruling on PR #110, 2026-07-14). The static scan (guest/linux/scan-counter-opcodes.sh) covers the built image, and CONFIG_MODULES asserted off means no loadable code escapes it — but a guest that mints executable code at runtime (a JIT, self-modifying code) could introduce a raw counter read the static scan never saw. Needed: vmm-side tracking of pages the guest makes executable (W^X enforcement / exec-permission interception at the KVM memslot or page-table level — contract work), re-scanning any newly executable page for the counter opcodes before it runs. Sharper on ARM (kill condition 2: no trap backstop exists there), so this should land before any non-fully-owned ARM guest; on x86 the retained RDTSC trap makes the gap survivable meanwhile.

comments.author: Paul Hemberger
comments.text:
Nested-KVM dev-loop probe (hm-8l3) -> REFUSE. TCG-only until Altra (hm-7pb).

This Mac is an Apple M1 Max on macOS 26.4.1. Virtualization.framework nested virt needs M3+ AND macOS 15+; the macOS gate passes but M1 is pre-M3. Confirmed directly against the host API: VZGenericPlatformConfiguration.isNestedVirtualizationSupported = false. So an aarch64 Linux guest on this machine cannot expose a hardware /dev/kvm — the KVM ioctl loop (KVM_CREATE_VM / KVM_CREATE_VCPU / KVM_RUN) is unreachable locally.

Consequence for this ARM backend skeleton: pure ARM logic runs natively (this Mac is aarch64), but there is NO local KVM ioctl/boot dev loop. QEMU TCG is the fallback oracle for the ioctl/boot path until the Ampere Altra box (hm-7pb) is racked and reachable. Plan the dev loop accordingly: native unit/logic tests + TCG smoke locally, real KVM validation on Altra.

title: Implement the paravirt work-derived clock, x86-first (PARAVIRT-CLOCK.md ABI v1)
description: Ratified-to-build by the 2026-07-13 pre-build ruling (Paul; docs/ARCH-BOUNDARY.md, Pre-build ruling section): implement docs/PARAVIRT-CLOCK.md on x86 first — the materialized work-derived clock page (seqlock ABI v1), guest-kernel clocksource/sched_clock/delay paths routed through the page, RDTSC trap RETAINED underneath as the enforcement backstop and oracle, canonical re-stamp at seal/snapshot quiescent points per the spec 1.1 hazards. The x86 payoff is RDTSC exits leaving the hot path (the nested-x86 N-4 memo lever); live-validate on the Intel box: determinism gates bit-identical with the page active, plus a measured exit-count reduction. ARM closure (CNTKCTL_EL1/CNTHCTL_EL2 posture + counter-read opcode scan) is stage AA-5 validation on silicon, NOT this bead. Sequenced behind hm-b5n because both churn vmm-core (the merge-window rule); the ABI details freeze through this implementation PR review.
notes:
Round 4 fixer RESPAWNED on Opus 4.8 2026-07-14 ~17:20 after two consecutive Fable-5 safeguard false-positive blocks killed the original session's turns (kernel/VMM content). Same branch/worktree; briefed via PR record (statelessness held). Round-4 scope: seqlock ABA at seal, page-off v3 blob shape, G3 tick attribution, bzImage boot-artifact scan.
r4 (cross-model, head ade2763): 3 P1 + 1 P2, all fixed on task/paravirt-clock-x86.

(1) SEAL-TIME SEQLOCK ABA (P1) — RULING CHANGE, flagged for veto. The bead's own
description says 'canonical re-stamp at seal/snapshot quiescent points per the spec
1.1 hazards'. That is NOT SAFELY IMPLEMENTABLE and is now amended in
docs/PARAVIRT-CLOCK.md 1.1. Resetting a LIVE seqlock epoch to a fixed canonical
value is an ABA: a reader that sampled seq=0, took an exit before its validating
re-read, and resumed after a refresh-then-canonicalize sees seq=0 again and accepts
pre-refresh values — taking a snapshot changes the guest's future. The doc's safety
premise ('a seal is taken at an HLT quiescent Moment') has been FALSE since task 41
(seals happen at any V-time-synchronized intercept). Canonicalizing only the
snapshot COPY (the reviewer's suggested fix) was also rejected: it makes the sealed
image differ from live guest RAM, breaking snapshot_derive (which diffs live RAM
against the parent IMAGE) and same-state=>same-future (a parent that seals and
continues would diverge, by exactly its seq, from a child restored from its own
snapshot). RESOLUTION: the page is sealed VERBATIM. History-freedom comes from
value-keyed stamping (r1) — the epoch advances only on distinct-value publications,
so it is already a pure function of the deterministic execution, and a restored run
inherits its parent's epoch. Canonical form survives as the REGISTRATION form only.
save_vm_state is &self again (mutates nothing) => this PR no longer changes that
public signature at all.

(2) Device blob (P1): the version is now the offer flag — unoffered VMs encode v3
byte-identical to main (page-off really is byte-identical, at the wire); only
enable_pvclock compositions encode v4. main's v3 blobs still decode.

(3) G3 vacuity (P1): the 100Hz tick already refreshes the page every ~10ms, which
is ALSO the default Delta — max_gap<=Delta would have passed with the forced refresh
DELETED. G3 now runs at Delta=tick/10 and asserts the new
Vmm::pvclock_forced_landings() (landings where neither timer nor arrival was due)
dominate the window. A portable test proves a timer-caused landing is NOT counted.

(4) bzImage scan gap (P2): bzImage is 3 executable artifacts and all 3 run; only
vmlinux was scanned. All 3 now are, artifact-qualified so same-named symbols cannot
alias budgets. setup + decompressor have ZERO counter reads — confirmed by real
disassembly (4,846/5,988 insns) AND a raw byte search for 0F31/0F01F9 (the real-mode
16-bit decode caveat). Armed scan verified green, and verified to FAIL on a planted
site and on a stale decompressor entry.

Gates: workspace nextest 1732 passed; clippy -D warnings clean on mac + x86_64-linux
+ aarch64; fmt; deny; vtime Miri 10/10. public-api snapshot regenerated ON THE BOX
(the vmm-core public_api test is Linux-frozen, skips on mac). Box G0-G3/perf window
still outstanding — unchanged.
r5 (cross-model, head 328bcff): 4 P1 + 2 P2. The box-gates P1 is the task's own
standing merge condition (G1/G2/G3 + perf in a foreman-granted window), NOT a fix — recorded,
outstanding. Five portable fixes landed:

(1) REGISTRATION CAPABILITY for pre-registration snapshots (P1). A snapshot sealed before the
guest registered carries no GPA, so the deterministic-backend check was skipped entirely; restore
onto a non-deterministic backend and the guest's next pvclock_register (which the SOURCE accepted)
answers UnknownService = same state, different future. The v4 blob now carries the source's
'registrable' bit (Vmm::pvclock_available) and restore requires EQUALITY. The prior test asserted
the bug; it is now the regression pin.

(2) DETERMINISTIC FIRST-ARM (P1). A guest that registers and immediately busy-waits took none of
the intercepts the Delta deadline waited for => page frozen forever. pvclock_register now anchors
V-time from a fresh work read (the doorbell OUT is a synchronous instruction trap, exact like
RDTSC) and arms the deadline THERE. The r2 overdue hazard is retired by an invariant
(run_until-bounded entries can't overshoot anchor+Delta), not by waiting. first_advance_seen
deleted. The kernel's courtesy rdtsc is no longer load-bearing.

(3) G3 WAS VACUOUS (P1). The date shell loop syscalls, and syscall entry reads the TSC (kstack
randomization, do_syscall_64 allowlisted) => every syscall refreshed the page for free. G3 now
runs guest/linux/pvclock-spin.c: mmaps the page via /dev/mem, spins on seqlock reads with NO
syscalls/traps in the loop, reports PVSPIN_DONE (asserted). Verified: -Wall -Wextra -Werror
static, read_vns has 0 syscall/rdtsc insns, ships in the exec image (built+unpacked+executed).

(4) LAPIC MMIO HOLE (P2). map_memory splits memslots around [0xFEE00000,+0x1000); a page-aligned
GPA there passed the RAM-bound check while guest loads hit the LAPIC model. Rejected now via a new
Vendor::mmio_holes() seam (naming x86 MMIO is vendor knowledge, ARCH-BOUNDARY).

(5) UnknownService BEFORE classification (P2): the doorbell graded pvclock requests
(BadRequest/UnknownOpcode) before the availability gate, leaking the service on compositions that
keep the doorbell alive for another channel. Availability checked first now.

Gates: workspace nextest 1735 passed; clippy -D warnings mac+x86_64-linux+aarch64; fmt; deny;
public-api regenerated on the box (Vendor::mmio_holes delta). Miri re-running. Box G0-G3/perf
window still outstanding (the standing merge condition).

(1) PVCK now folds pvclock_available() (P1) — two offered VMs differing only in deterministic_clock
had identical state_hash though one can register and one answers UnknownService. (2) decode rejects
the impossible (delta, Some(gpa), false) tuple (P1) — would else commit an active registration onto
a target the capability check refuses. (3) G1 live arm negotiates Hello before Run/Snapshot (P1) —
else Unsupported panics before the hash compare. (4) registration restores vtime_synchronized (P2) —
else a snapshot right after register is spuriously NotQuiescent. (5) Postgres perf arm requires a
complete window: no step error + final V-time>=window (P2) — else truncated partial counts pass as

  page bytes hashed in full => zero refresh/canonicalization entropy leaks into guest RAM.

PERF (kill condition 3), reported honestly: x86 RDTSC-exit-rate reduction ~1.03x (Postgres steady
state) / 1.02x (boot) — BELOW the 2x threshold. NOT a mechanism failure (clocksource IS selected):
the exits the page removes (clocksource .read()) are a small fraction of total RDTSC traffic, which

DISCOVERED PRE-EXISTING FINDING (for foreman, NOT a pvclock regression): det-corpus O2 insn-cpuid
FAILS on this box — the digest is DETERMINISTIC run-to-run (identical) but != the committed golden.

PV_PERF_WINDOW_VNS=3e8). INITRAMFS_EXEC_SHA256=7f691432.

P1 (on_deadline overdue anchor): the r7 anchor-taint family's last site. A pvclock deadline armed
off a stale anchor (>Delta since last intercept) is born overdue, and on the REAL backend the
overdue AtOrPastDeadline path returns reached = a live PMU count (skid); on_deadline promoted it
into last_intercept_work -> next page stamp + state hash. Fix: on_deadline anchors to the
deterministic run_until TARGET (threaded from step), not reached. target==reached for normal
landings, always <= reached, so deterministic + monotone. The mock rewrites reached:=deadline so
the portable suite never saw it; new direct on_deadline test proves the anchor+page are identical

BOX RE-VALIDATION (final head, default invocations, no overrides):

*** PERF CORRECTION (major) ***: kill condition 3 PASSES ~25x, NOT the ~1x I reported earlier.
The workload-relative measurement (r8 P2d) shows page-off 1399 rdtsc exits vs page-on 56 over the
actual Postgres workload = 24.95x reduction (page removes ~96% of workload RDTSC exits). The
earlier ~1x was a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT: cumulative-from-boot, swamped by pre-registration TSC
calibration (identical in both arms; the harmony clocksource only takes over at early_initcall).
So on x86 the page IS worth it for steady-state timekeeping. IMPLEMENTATION + PR updated.

r8 (2nd pass, cross-model on head 84985f1): 1 P1 + 2 P2. The P1 resolved by the foreman's
REGISTRATION HANDSHAKE ruling, which supersedes the r5/r6/r7 registration-anchor iterations.

RULING: the doorbell OUT + the guest's REQUIRED post-doorbell RDTSC together are the registration
handshake. OUT records a PENDING registration (no stamp, no arm — it is a PIO, skid-tainted, and
the pre-OUT anchor may be stale). The first stamp + Delta arm happen only at the handshake
intercept (a genuine skid-free RDTSC), off a fresh anchor that can never be born overdue.
Non-handshaking guests are OUT OF CONTRACT (stale-but-deterministic page, no refresh). This roots
out the overdue-live-count path entirely (pvclock deadline can no longer be born overdue).

Host: PvclockChannel::armed; pending at OUT; promote+stamp+arm at first vtime_synchronized
step-tail; restore arms immediately (anchor 0 synchronized). The r8 on_deadline target-anchor
change is KEPT (makes vtime_synchronized => deterministic anchor hold universally, which the
handshake stamp relies on).

*** THE BOX CAUGHT A REAL KERNEL BUG ***: the comment-only patch edit was INSUFFICIENT. First box
re-validation showed 'harmony_pvclock: ABI mismatch (page says 0) refusing the page' -> fell back
to TSC. The kernel validates the page's abi_version/flags right after registration but BEFORE its
handshake rdtsc; with the host deferring the stamp to the handshake, the page was unstamped at
validation. FIX: reorder the kernel so the handshake rdtsc PRECEDES the ABI validation. This
changed the bzImage (051de137 -> e4591ea8); rebuilt on the box, MANIFEST re-pinned; both initramfs
reproduced bit-identically. Still 2 rdtscs (allowlist unchanged).

FULL BOX RE-VALIDATION on the reordered kernel (all GREEN): G0 smoke PASS with clocksource
correctly 'Switched to clocksource harmony-pvclock'; G1 3/3 seals bit-identical; G2 PASS (oracle +
deliberate-fault); G3 PASS (1921/2182=88% forced by Delta); Postgres workload perf 24.90x
reduction (page-off 1399 vs page-on 56, boot excluded) — the ~25x kill-condition PASS HOLDS with
the handshake + correct clocksource selection.

title: [bug] SIGSTOP-cycling wedge (nested-x86 spike finding)
description: Found during the nested-x86 spike N-3 pause/resume conditions (2026-07-10): SIGSTOP/SIGCONT cycling can wedge the stack. Evidence in spikes/nested-x86 results (spike/nested-x86 branch). Reproduce on main, then either fix the wedge or make it fail closed (detected + refused, never a silent hang). Relevant to any future host that suspends the process (cloud migration rehearsal was the motivating condition).
notes:
DIAGNOSIS (tasks/114): spike wedge is QEMU-nested-harness surface (L1 QEMU KVM_RUN), but the ANALOGOUS wedge lives in a shipping crate. run_until = vmm-backend::drive_run_until -> vtime::InjectionPlanner::stop_at. Phase-2 loop 'while current < target { single_step }' (vtime/src/planner.rs) is UNBOUNDED — the module doc literally admits 'A guest that never retires another counted event would step forever'. Under SIGSTOP-cycling a lost work-clock completion (vPMU overflow PMI / MTF) stalls counted-event progress -> silent infinite single-step loop = the hang the bead forbids. This is pure logic, portably reachable (issues no syscall; tested vs SimCpu), so mock-repro + fix land portably. The Phase-1 variant (overflow lost -> run_until_overflow KVM_RUN never returns) is a BLOCKED IOCTL in box-only kvm_sys.rs, not reachable in pure logic — separate disposition (needs ioctl watchdog). FIX: fail-closed step budget (consecutive zero-progress single-steps) -> new VtimeError::StepBudgetExceeded, mapped to a loud BackendError in drive_run_until. Never a silent hang.
IMPLEMENTED on branch task/sigstop-cycling-wedge (commit e364268, NOT pushed — foreman opens/reviews the PR). FIX: fail-closed step budget in vtime::InjectionPlanner::stop_at (new PlannerConfig.max_stall_steps + VtimeError::StepBudgetExceeded), mapped to a loud BackendError::Internal in vmm-backend::drive_run_until; production STALL_STEP_BUDGET=1<<24. Turns the unbounded single-step walk (the shipping analogue of the spike wedge) from a silent hang into a typed refusal; reaching-path behaviour byte-identical. 4 portable mock regression tests assert bounded-not-hung. Disposition: shipping single-step wedge EXPOSED->fixed; QEMU L1 wedge = not our code; residual Phase-1 blocked-KVM_RUN (overflow lost) = box-only ioctl watchdog, out of scope (named in IMPLEMENTATION-task114.md). Gates green: workspace nextest 1696 passed/29 skipped, clippy(vtime+vmm-backend all-targets), fmt, deny. Substantive-tier (touches run_until seam) — expect cross-model review.
r1 (PR #113, pushed f82dba2): (1) reverted to source-compatible design — PlannerConfig frozen contract untouched; backstop now InjectionPlanner::new default (DEFAULT_MAX_STALL_STEPS=1<<24, on by default) + with_max_stall_steps builder; public-api = additions not break; dropped vmm-backend STALL_STEP_BUDGET. (2) no QUEUE.md hunk on branch. (3) Phase-1 blocked-ioctl residual REFUTED (72.7% Rl = spinning not blocked); IMPLEMENTATION corrected. Gates green: ws nextest 1696/29, clippy, fmt, deny. title: [bug] Marker filter has a hole: the guest's crash lines mint template species
description:
Found by tasks/97's offline re-key (bead hm-b3h), proven over all 40 bug-3 campaigns.

conductor::benchcampaign::cells_of filters the bug's serial marker (UUID_BUG) out of the console BEFORE clustering, precisely so the log-template signal cannot key its own attribution marker as novelty (the round-6 P1 fix). But the kernel's fault message rides immediately BEHIND the marker and is not filtered:

    UUID_BUG: rare-entropy prefix matched; poisoning pointer     <- filtered
    [ 0.383925] traps: uuid-super[129] general protection fault  <- NOT filtered

So the log-template sensor mints a 4th template species from the crash itself. Consequence, verified on the corpus: in EVERY one of the 29 finding campaigns the 4th species debuts EXACTLY on the finding branch, and in every one of the 11 non-finders the archive is frozen at 3 cells from branch 0 for all 512 branches. v1's entire post-genesis novelty on bug 3 is a post-hoc crash artifact — it arrives only after the bug has been found, so it can never steer a search.

This also means CORRELATION-REPORT.md's rho = -0.671 (cells@256 vs TTB) is a restatement of 'did this campaign find the bug before branch 256?', not a graded novelty<->progress relationship. That report already suspected the statistic was degenerate; the re-key proves the mechanism. It does NOT change the NO-GO ruling (the signal was worse than baseline on find rate regardless).

The fix is a one-line discipline, not a redesign: filter post-crash console output before clustering, or — better and more general — key only on records at or before the seal. Any future campaign whose guest crashes noisily will otherwise key its own crash as novelty and inflate every correlation it computes.
acceptance_criteria: A campaign's cell function cannot mint a species from output the guest produced after (or as part of) the crash that ends the run. Land this BEFORE the next correlation campaign; a re-key of the frozen corpus under the fix is free (cargo run -p rekey).
notes: Evidence: dissonance/benchmark/REKEY-REPORT.md, section 'Why v1 is blind: the fourth cell IS the crash'. Gated in dissonance/rekey/tests/corpus.rs::v1s_only_post_genesis_cell_is_the_crash.

title: Probe: nested KVM inside an aarch64 Linux VM on the M-series Mac (ARM dev-loop question)
description: One bounded probe from the 2026-07-13 pre-build ruling: can an aarch64 Linux VM on this Mac expose /dev/kvm (nested virtualization) well enough for the ARM backend ioctl/boot dev loop? (Virtualization.framework nested virt needs macOS 15+ on M3-or-later — record the actual chip and path tried, e.g. UTM/vz.) Deliverable: a GO/refuse note recorded on the ARM-skeleton bead plus a setup recipe if GO; QEMU TCG stays the fallback oracle either way. Zero box time, zero spend, an hour of work.
close_reason:
VERDICT: REFUSE — nested KVM is unavailable on this Mac. QEMU TCG stays the only local ARM oracle until the Ampere Altra box (hm-7pb) arrives.

HOST FACTS (2026-07-15):
- Chip: Apple M1 Max (hw.model MacBookPro18,2) — M1 generation
- macOS: 26.4.1 (build 25E253) — satisfies the macOS 15+ gate
- arch: arm64

GATE HIT: Apple's Virtualization.framework nested virtualization requires an M3-or-later chip AND macOS 15+. The macOS gate passes (26.4.1 >> 15) but the CHIP gate FAILS — M1 Max is two generations below M3. Hardware limit; no software workaround exists.

EVIDENCE — authoritative host-API check (not just chip-name inference):
  $ cat nestcheck.swift
  import Virtualization
  if #available(macOS 15.0, *) {
      print("isNestedVirtualizationSupported = \(VZGenericPlatformConfiguration.isNestedVirtualizationSupported)")
  }
  $ swift nestcheck.swift
  VZGenericPlatformConfiguration.isNestedVirtualizationSupported = false

Because macOS 26.4.1 already provides the nested-virt API, the `false` return is the framework reporting that the M1 hardware cannot do nested virtualization — the definitive answer straight from the platform, on this exact machine.

REFUSAL POINT / METHOD: Stopped at method step 1 (host-facts) per the spec's step-3 rule ("pre-M3 chip -> STOP, record REFUSE, do not chase workarounds"). No VM bring-up attempted: the host framework already reports nested virt unsupported, so any aarch64 Linux guest here would fall back to TCG and could never expose a hardware-accelerated /dev/kvm. There is no ioctl transcript because the /dev/kvm loop is physically unreachable on this hardware.

CONSEQUENCE for hm-cbt (ARM backend skeleton): the local KVM ioctl/boot dev loop is NOT available on this Mac. Pure ARM logic still runs natively (the Mac is aarch64), but the KVM ioctl loop (KVM_CREATE_VM / KVM_CREATE_VCPU / KVM_RUN) requires the Altra box (hm-7pb). QEMU TCG is the sanctioned fallback oracle for the ioctl/boot path until then.

INSTALLS / REVERTS: NONE. swift/swiftc were already present (/usr/bin via CommandLineTools); no brew/lima/UTM installs. Zero box time, zero spend, zero repo working-tree changes.

title: generic Explorer::modulation should skip/retry inadmissible proposals
description:
control_error_to_machine (explorer/src/adapter.rs) maps a well-formed-but-rejected fault PROPOSAL to the distinct MachineError::Inadmissible variant (PerturbOutOfRange / PerturbPastMoment / PerturbMomentTaken / Unsupported) precisely so a proposing loop CAN discard the proposal and continue rather than aborting. But only the benchmark campaign loop (conductor::benchcampaign) actually handles that variant today. The generic Explorer::modulation still treats Inadmissible as terminal and aborts — so a generic exploration driver that proposes an out-of-range/stale fault dies instead of skipping it. Add skip/retry (or configurable propose-again) handling for MachineError::Inadmissible to the generic Explorer path so it degrades like the benchmark loop.

## Context
Discovered during task-69 M2 PR#90 final review: the adapter.rs comment claimed 'a proposing driver (explorer, benchmark campaign) discards the proposal and continues', but that is only true for the benchmark loop; the generic Explorer::modulation propagates Inadmissible as an error and aborts. The comment was narrowed to the truth in the same commit; this bead tracks the actual generic-Explorer capability gap. The spine (Explorer::modulation) is outside task-69's surface.
